status_summary: No separation has occurred; the administration has kept one officer in both roles. President Trump ordered the firing of Gen. Timothy Haugh, who led both organizations, in April 2025, and The Record reported on 2025-05-14 that the administration had not decided on a split, that the acting leader and the Joint Chiefs Chairman favored keeping the dual-hat, and that the White House would nominate one officer for both roles or a three-star officer for Cyber Command alone. On 2026-03-10 the Senate confirmed Gen. Joshua Rudd, 71 to 29 (Senate roll call vote 49 on PN711; cloture was invoked 68 to 28 on 2026-03-09), and the Washington Examiner reports that he will lead NSA and also serve as dual-hat leader of Cyber Command, after a year without Senate-confirmed leadership. Under an earlier defense policy law, as described by The Record, a split requires the Defense Secretary and the Joint Chiefs Chairman to certify jointly that it will not hinder Cyber Command's effectiveness; no certification or separation plan was found. The Record reported on 2025-09-09, citing unnamed sources, that senior officials had dropped a possible split without a formal presidential document, judging it too lengthy, while a White House official said no long-term decisions had been made. At his 2026-01-15 confirmation hearing the nominee for both posts cited the arrangement's effectiveness and said he would keep assessing it; SecurityWeek reports the March 2026 confirmation was to lead both organizations. No decision to split, certification or separation plan was found through 2026-10-12.

timeline.event: The Record reports that weeks after Gen. Haugh's firing the administration had not decided whether to split the roles; acting leader Lt. Gen. Hartman and Chairman Gen. Caine favored keeping the dual-hat, and a split would require a joint certification under an earlier defense policy law.

The Record reports, citing unnamed sources, that senior officials dropped a possible split of the roles without a presidential memo, judging that ending the dual-hat could take up to three years; a White House official said no long-term decisions had been made. It adds that the Defense Secretary told senators in June 2025 that the status quo held while reserving the right to review it, and that the Joint Chiefs Chairman wrote that the arrangement should remain.

At his Senate Armed Services confirmation hearing, Lt. Gen. Joshua Rudd, nominated to lead both NSA and Cyber Command, cites the arrangement's effectiveness and says he would keep assessing whether the dual-hat is the most effective structure; no decision or timeline is reported.

The Senate confirms Lt. Gen. Joshua M. Rudd (PN711) to be a general in the Army, 71 to 29, on roll call vote 49 (cloture had been invoked 68 to 28 on 2026-03-09). The Washington Examiner reports he will lead both the National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command in a dual-hat arrangement after about a year without Senate-confirmed leaders at both agencies. SecurityWeek (2026-03-11) also reports the confirmation covers leading both organizations.

uncertainties: I did not find a DOD or White House statement on the dual-hat decision or the date Rudd was nominated; his confirmation testimony on the dual-hat is known from a DefenseScoop report, not the hearing record. The Senate roll call records (votes 48 and 49) show the cloture and confirmation votes on PN711 for Lt. Gen. Rudd to be a general in the Army; that the post is NSA Director and Cyber Command commander in a dual-hat arrangement rests on the Washington Examiner report, which the roll call does not state. The vote date is 2026-03-10 (the 2026-03-09 date in the earlier version was the cloture vote). The Haugh firing is dated only as April 2025 from The Record. The statutory certification rule is described from 2017 and 2024 articles, not the current statute text, and I did not check whether the FY2026 NDAA changed it. Stage 'diverged' reflects that, at a vacancy where separate nominations were an open option, the administration nominated and the Senate confirmed one officer for both roles; if the dual-hat is later ended, the record should change.
